findings: Grouping searches only the current first-byte hash bucket and its two lexical neighbors among occupied buckets. Lexical adjacency is not a complete Hamming-radius search; low-distance hashes can be missed across other buckets.

Image predicate accepts hammingDistance <= threshold without rejecting -1, so malformed hashes can pass the hash gate if histogram comparison succeeds. Video any-frame predicate has the same invalid-distance issue.

fullHashMap begins as all cached entries. If a changed item fails rehash, its old entry is not removed before grouping, and current paths still include it; stale hashes can therefore be used despite a failed refresh. Source-only finding.

Greedy grouping compares candidates only to each anchor and marks group members visited. It is order dependent and neither all-pairs clique validation nor full connected-component traversal. Pairwise denial checks only anchor/candidate, not every member pair.

Groups sharing an anchor pHash are merged by string group ID, potentially joining separately denied/incompatible sets. For videos the ID uses only first-frame hash while comparison accepts any frame pair.
Video sampling uses nearest sync frames at 10% and 50% duration; any similar frame pair qualifies, without duration/order/coverage validation. Source does not establish full-video equivalence.

Parallel worker coroutines append failures to a shared mutableList without synchronization. Null hash results are omitted without adding skipped-path diagnostics. Cancellation and actual race effects require runtime qualification.

Image histogram is 64-bin RGB from 16x16 scaled bitmap, alpha ignored. Malformed counts parse to zero and all-zero histograms compare equal. Bitmap scaling may alias originals; recycling ownership depends on Android scale semantics and remains unqualified.
